seoTitle: How to Create a Confluence Page from Jira
metaDescription: Create a Confluence page directly from a Jira work item, using the built-in editor to add content and publish without leaving Jira.
intro: When Jira and Confluence share the same Atlassian workspace, you don't have to leave a work item just to start writing documentation about it — an editor opens right there, lets you build out a page, and hands you a Publish button when it's ready. This guide walks through that flow starting from an open work item, through the Confluence editor that appears, to publishing the finished page.

steps.heading: Open the Jira work item you want to document
steps.body: Click into the item — in this walkthrough, a task called "TEST work" (TPT-10) — which opens its full view with Description, Subtasks, Linked work items, and an Activity section on the left, and a Details panel on the right showing Assignee, Reporter, Priority, and similar metadata. This is the item whatever Confluence page you create will end up tied back to.

image.caption: An open Jira work item, TEST work (TPT-10), showing its description, activity, and details panel before any Confluence content is attached.

steps.heading: Start creating Confluence content from the item
steps.body: From the icons near the top of the item, next to the title, there's a create-content control that opens Confluence content creation directly inside Jira rather than sending you to a separate tab. This is the built-in link between the two products — it only works if your Jira and Confluence sites are part of the same Atlassian workspace.

steps.heading: Work inside the Confluence editor that opens
steps.body: A panel titled "Open In Confluence" appears with a full rich-text toolbar — text styles, formatting, tables, emoji, and more — sitting above a live page draft. In this example the page is titled "JIRA TASKS - Confluence," attributed to the same user who owns the Jira item, giving you a real editor rather than a stripped-down preview.

image.caption: The Confluence editor opened from inside Jira, mid-draft on a page titled "JIRA TASKS - Confluence," with a Publish button ready.

steps.heading: Add structured content, not just text
steps.body: The editor supports more than paragraphs — the draft shown here has an embedded database block titled "Untitled database 2026-07-01" inserted directly into the page, with a confirmation toast noting "Database added under this content" and an option to open it in a new tab for easier editing. That's worth knowing if your documentation needs more structure than plain notes, such as tracking a table of related decisions or test cases alongside the issue.

steps.heading: Write the actual documentation
steps.body: Fill in whatever the issue actually needs recorded — meeting notes, a spec, acceptance criteria, or a summary of a decision made in the comments. Since the page lives in Confluence once published, treat it like any other Confluence page: give it a clear title people can find later, not just a name that only makes sense next to the Jira item it started from.

steps.heading: Publish the page
steps.body: Click Publish in the top right of the editor to finalize it. Once published, the page exists as a normal Confluence page in whatever space it was created under, and it stays referenced back to the Jira item it was created from — so anyone opening the issue later can find the documentation without having to search Confluence separately.

steps.heading: Check visibility if teammates can't see it
steps.body: A newly published page inherits the permissions of its Confluence space, which may be more restrictive than the Jira project it's linked from. If a teammate can open the Jira item but not the linked Confluence page, that's a space-permission issue, not a broken link — check the space's access settings rather than recreating the page.

faq.question: Do Jira and Confluence need to be connected first?
faq.answer: Yes, this only works when your Jira and Confluence sites are part of the same Atlassian workspace, which is how the create-content control ends up available directly inside a work item.

faq.question: Can I add more than text to the Confluence page?
faq.answer: Yes. The editor supports rich formatting and structured content blocks — the example here embeds a database block directly into the page, not just plain paragraphs.

faq.question: Will changes to the Jira issue update the linked Confluence page?
faq.answer: No. The two stay linked for reference, but content on each is independent — editing the Jira item afterward won't change anything already published on the Confluence page.

faq.question: Who can see the newly created Confluence page?
faq.answer: Visibility depends on the permissions of the Confluence space the page is published into, which can be more restrictive than the Jira project — check space access if a teammate can't open it.

faq.question: Do I have to publish immediately, or can I keep drafting?
faq.answer: The editor lets you keep working before hitting Publish — the page shown mid-draft here already had content and a database block added before the final publish step.
